headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/cascading-error from mem0 outputs being reused by a content-writing agent; no direct data-leak or capability-conflict pathway is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management agent and python-cheatsheet is a content-writing/reference agent; if mem0 outputs are copied into the writer’s prompt or draft, the writer may treat them as trusted text. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from roles and remains uncertain, but the interaction is plausible.
conditions: IF mem0 outputs are pasted or piped into python-cheatsheet prompts without provenance markers, injection risk exists.
IF an orchestrator bridges the agents through shared text fields, the writer may follow attacker-controlled instructions.
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and provenance label before any mem0 text is reused.
Strip imperative phrases from mem0 outputs before passing them onward.
Require a human review step for any copied instructions.
Use separate workspaces or message channels for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware prompt templating.

B_data_leakage.rationale: mem0 reports network_egress none and python-cheatsheet has no files, clipboard, or stdin/stdout surfaces plus no secrets handled. With no shared workspace or upload path documented, there is no plausible pairwise leakage route in the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced outside these profiles, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is later granted network egress or file access, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents offline.
Do not mount a shared workspace.
Avoid passing secrets into either agent.
Re-check the profiles if IO surfaces change.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 exposes no write or shell capability in the profile, while python-cheatsheet explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, subprocess, and shell execution. Without overlapping mutable-resource writes, there is no capability conflict pathway to score.
conditions: IF mem0 is deployed with additional write or git permissions not shown here, conflict risk must be reassessed.
IF python-cheatsheet gains write access through an external wrapper, overlap could emerge.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only.
Do not grant mem0 filesystem or git write permissions.
Run each agent in separate processes.
Audit any wrapper that adds mutable-resource access.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway exists if mem0’s memory output is fed into python-cheatsheet as authoritative content, because the latter is a content-writing agent and may render or reuse the text without verification. The profiles do not show explicit validation or provenance checks, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet uses mem0 output as source text without a verification step, cascading error occurs.
IF the orchestrator auto-inserts mem0 memory into drafts, the risk is active.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before reuse.
Mark mem0 output as untrusted source material.
Require citations for any factual claims copied over.
Limit mem0 output to bullet summaries.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies are documented for either agent, and both profiles show no secrets handled or data classes touched. With no compliance mismatch evidence, there is no basis for a compliance finding.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency or retention policies are added, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Record retention settings for both agents.
Avoid regulated data until policies are defined.
